What makes the honeybee so amazing?

The hardworking honeybee is a social insect that lives together around a queen bee. The way it makes honey and talks through dance is truly amazing!

We've gathered all kinds of stories about honeybees — honeybee facts, the honeybee dance, and honeybee pollination.

content.alt: Honeybee - Nature and science facts about the honeybee
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the honeybee

Worker bees sip nectar from flowers, gather it, and turn it into honey in the hive, carrying pollen in the "pollen baskets" on their hind legs. As they travel from flower to flower this way, they help with pollination, making them a very important insect that lets many of the fruits and vegetables we eat grow. When one finds a good flower patch, it does the amazing thing of telling its hive-mates where it is with a "waggle dance".

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Connect "honeybees help flowers so fruit can grow" to the fruit you eat. Act out the waggle dance with your body, and watch honeybees from a distance in a flower garden to make it even more exciting (be careful not to get stung).

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why are honeybees so important?
A. As they travel from flower to flower they help with pollination, letting many of the fruits and vegetables we eat grow.

Q. What is the waggle dance?
A. It's how a bee tells its hive-mates where it found a good flower patch. It dances in a figure-eight shape.

Q. How can we observe it at home?
A. Connect it to the fruit you eat, act out the waggle dance, and watch from a distance in a flower garden (without getting stung).
